land.text: the French Vexin, annexed to the royal domain by Philip I in 1082

capitals.name: Pontoise
capitals.note: The Vexin page names Pontoise as the Vexin's capital.

keyframe_review.note: 4,130 km2 with a bbox of 1.4-3.6 E, 48.5-49.3 N, a span (220 km) far larger than an area of that size needs, so the outline is probably several pieces; not checked. The Vexin page gives no area figure but describes the Vexin as 'roughly rectangular, measuring about 40 by 35 kilometres' (about 1,400 km2), so the shape is about three times the Vexin, beyond the factor of two; unresolved (eu-10-c reviewer). It says the Vexin was split by the Epte in 911 into a French (east) and a Norman (west) Vexin and that in 1031 Robert I of Normandy 'received the French Vexin between the Epte and Oise, including Pontoise' from Henry I: the French Vexin was thus a Norman grant from 1031, with counts (Gauthier III to 1063, then Ralph IV of Valois) in place; whether the shape is the French Vexin or both is not on the page. Unverified, kept as drawn.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape unchanged but holding only to 1082: 'Philip I seized the chance to reclaim the French Vexin' in 1082

keyframe_review.note: 4,130 km2, the same outline. Years only: Cliopatria keeps the county to 1084; the Vexin page and the Philip I page both date the annexation to 1082. Ralph IV's only son Simon de Vexin entered a monastery in 1077, leaving the county without an heir.

region.text: the county of the Vexin, Cliopatria's 990 outline; the Vexin page names Pontoise as its capital

ledger.note: 990: the County of Vexin, with Pontoise, enters the record. Page silent on the county's origin beyond the 911 split of the Vexin by the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte; 990 is Cliopatria's first year for the row.

1063: Gauthier III de Gouy dies a prisoner of William the Bastard and his cousin Ralph IV of Valois succeeds him as count of the Vexin. 'Gauthier III de Gouy was poisoned and died a prisoner of William the Bastard. His cousin Ralph IV of Valois succeeded him.' Same county, a new house.

region.text: the French Vexin, reclaimed by Philip I and added to the royal domain

ledger.note: 1082: Philip I annexes the Vexin. 'Philip I seized the chance to reclaim the French Vexin, which his father had granted to the Duke of Normandy'; the Philip I page: 'expanded his demesne with the annexation of the Vexin' in 1082. Ralph IV's only son Simon de Vexin had entered a monastery in 1077.

wars.name: Contest for the French Vexin between Philip I and William the Conqueror

zones.text: the French Vexin, between the Epte and Oise

wars.outcome: After Philip I's annexation of 1082 William, as duke of Normandy, 'pillaged the French Vexin in summer [1087], clashed with Philip I, and was fatally injured in the assault on Mantes'; the Vexin stayed with the crown.
wars.note: The county itself ends in 1082; the war is listed because the zone stays disputed to 1087. The Philip I page dates the annexation to 1082 'in reprisal against Robert Curthose's attack on William's heir' without saying which Vexin.

certainty.note: A small feudal county drawn from Cliopatria's outline; the Epte is the western frontier with Normandy (911 treaty) but no page gives a surveyed line.

sources.title: Vexin
sources.note: 911 split, 1031 Robert I of Normandy receives the French Vexin, 1063 Ralph IV, 1077 Simon, 1082 Philip I, 1087 Mantes, 1193-1195 Philip II; capital Pontoise; no area.

sources.title: Philip I of France
sources.note: 1082 annexation of the Vexin; the page does not say which Vexin.

notes:
Short life, two pages (budget 1-2). The Norman grant of the French Vexin to Robert I in 1031 (Vexin page) makes the county a Norman dependency until 1082, but the pages opened say nothing about the status of the counts (Gauthier III, Ralph IV) under it; the duchy-of-normandy dossier should say whether to record a vassal_start (counterpart county-of-vexin, 1031-1082). Cliopatria's neighbours list Normandy adjacent in 990-1071 and Norman England in 1072-1084.
Not modelled: Simon de Vexin's monastic vows (1077) and the later fate of the Vexin (Philip II took Gisors in 1193 and annexed the French Vexin in 1195, Vexin page) - outside this state's life; the Norman Vexin (west of the Epte) is not Cliopatria's shape. The pages I tried for counts (Simon of Crépy, Ralph IV of Valois, Walter III) do not exist under those titles (url_not_found). Counterpart without a dossier: none. Gazetteer names needed: Pontoise (place; not in places.jsonl).
